data.body: Measured 2026-09-29 on the LAN critic (vLLM, ~35 generated tokens/s per request while serving two): 2371 chars 624 s, 5436 chars 1133 s, 8190 empty completion, 30000 timeout; reasoning_effort low / enable_thinking false come back off contract. So a 44k-char diff is ~9 sequential chunks x ~1000 s = ~2.5 h. vLLM batches concurrent requests, so aggregate throughput rises with concurrency while per-request speed drops far less. (a) [[reviewer]].max_concurrency (default 1 = today) runs up to N chunks at once, results assembled in chunk order; (b) total_budget_s applies to the wall clock, not the sum; (c) partial/unavailable accounting unchanged per chunk. Measure before/after on a real diff.

data.body: Bug Bd5b59f3894: _memory_sources accepts any source containing '/' as a path; a lesson seen_in that is a sentence reaches (repo/rel).is_file() and raises OSError Errno 36 in run_nemo_run, so verify never ran there. Fix: a source is a path only if it is one path-shaped token (no whitespace, bounded length); and a stat that raises OSError is 'not a path', never a crash or a vanished finding. Regression test: an imported lesson whose seen_in is a >255-char sentence with '/' -- verify_import returns a report; fails on current code with OSError.

data.body: Bug B259fd32dbd: enforce.installed only finds HOOK_MARKER in .git/hooks/<name>; a pre-commit-framework hook never carries it, so run_nemo_run (ddflow-check-commit / ddflow-check-msg local hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml) is told 'NOT installed ... NOTHING checks it' and exit 2. Fix: a framework-generated hook (the 'File generated by pre-commit' header) whose .pre-commit-config.yaml has a hook at that stage whose entry runs 'hooks check-commit' / 'hooks check-msg' counts as installed, and status says it is armed through pre-commit. Regression test: repo with such a config + generated hooks -> status reports both installed, exit 0; fails on current code.
data.title: hooks status recognises ddflow checks armed through the pre-commit framework (fixes bug B259fd32dbd)

data.body: Bug B438d336b24: 'Phase: NOPE.99' passes check-msg. Fix: the value of an item_trailer_keys trailer must be the id of an item in the queue (not removed); new [enforce].trailer_waivers = {key = [words]} declares keys that mark a commit shipping no item (run_nemo_run: Phase-ships = none|filing|recon|evidence|followup), whose value must be one of those words. A queue that cannot be read is exit 2 (could not run), never a pass. run_nemo_run's config gets the waiver map in the same change window. Regression test: NOPE.99 refused naming the key and value; a real id passes; Phase-ships: none passes with the waiver, Phase-ships: bogus refused; fails on current code.
data.title: The item trailer must name an item in the queue; a waiver key takes only its declared words (fixes bug B438d336b24)

data.body: Bug B45d5aa72fa: the importer never completes a phase. With --include-done a phase whose every imported task is done/closed (or that has no tasks and whose heading carries the done marker) must be imported completed with evidence naming the source; a phase with open tasks stays open. Without --include-done, the report must say how many ticked tasks per phase were left out so '0/3' is not read as 'nothing shipped'. Also a re-run of --include-done over an existing import must add the missing done tasks under existing phases (103.A/103.C under 103). Regression test on a fixture with a CLOSED phase, a partly-shipped phase and an open one; fails on current code.
data.title: import --include-done completes a finished phase; a plain import says which ticked tasks it left out (fixes bug B45d5aa72fa)

data.summary: check-commit's staged_paths runs 'git -C <primary> diff --cached' while git hands the hook the WORKTREE's GIT_INDEX_FILE, so it diffs the worktree index against the PRIMARY checkout's HEAD instead of the worktree's: every file master modified since the branch point is reported as staged (demonstrated in a scratch repo: master edits shared.txt, the worktree stages mine.txt, ddflow sees 'A mine.txt, M shared.txt'), and the branch's own already-committed changes too (run_nemo_run DDFLOWPOLICY.1 with nothing staged: '.ddflow/config.toml'). Under commit_without_lease=block a branch behind master is refused for files it never touched; under warn it gets false warnings. Fix: run the staged diff in the tree being committed (_this_worktree), not the resolved primary.

data.body: Bug Bba366d9893: staged_paths(repo) runs git -C <primary> diff --cached with the hook's GIT_INDEX_FILE (the worktree's index), comparing it to the primary's HEAD: files master changed since the branch point and the branch's own committed changes read as staged. Fix: every staged-path read in the commit hooks (check_commit, check_views, check_docs and any other staged_paths caller) runs in the tree being committed (_this_worktree / cwd) with that tree's HEAD. Regression test: primary + worktree; master modifies shared.txt after the branch point; the worktree stages only mine.txt under a lease covering mine.txt; with commit_without_lease=block and GIT_INDEX_FILE set as git sets it, check_commit returns 0 and staged_paths is exactly [mine.txt]; fails on current code. Blocks run_nemo_run DDFLOWPOLICY.2 (block).
data.title: check-commit diffs the index against the committing worktree's HEAD, not the primary's (fixes bug Bba366d9893)

data.summary: The evidence contract is vacuous on every surface: api/gates.record adds the MEASURED tree_sha and diff_stat to the evidence dict before G.record checks 'a gate in gates.evidence_required needs evidence to pass', so the dict is never empty and a bare 'gate record <id> <gate> --outcome passed' with no note, command or output is accepted for unit_tests, rubber_duck, critic, standards (and docs). Probe: init, phase add P1, 'ddflow gate record P1 docs --outcome passed' -> exit 0. The check must look at what the CALLER supplied (note/command/output/model), not the measured fields.

data.body: Found while adding the docs phase gate (B-docs-phase-gate): api/gates.record sets tree_sha and diff_stat before services.gates.record checks evidence, so 'not evidence' is never true and gates.evidence_required is enforced nowhere through the CLI or MCP. Regression test: a bare passed on an evidence-required gate exits non-zero; with --evidence it passes; the measured fields are still recorded.
data.title: Evidence-required gates refuse a bare pass again: judge the caller's evidence (note, command, output, model), not the fields ddflow measures itself (fixes the vacuous-evidence bug)

data.how: Template: pid=$!; end=$((SECONDS+3600)); while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null && [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do sleep 30; done. Keep output files in a per-agent scratch subfolder. Before reporting, list your background shells and stop any still running.
data.rule: Every background 'wait until done' loop has (1) a deadline (e.g. SECONDS-based, exit non-zero when hit), (2) a condition that fails when the watched process DIES, not only a marker the process writes on a clean exit (check the PID with kill -0, or pair the marker test with it), (3) no 'pgrep -f <text>' whose text is in the loop's own command line, and (4) is stopped (TaskStop / kill) before the agent hands back.
data.summary: Background wait loops need a deadline and a liveness check (not just a clean-exit marker), must never pgrep -f a string in their own command, and must be stopped before the agent reports; otherwise they poll for hours after the work is gone.
data.title: A background wait loop must end by itself: a deadline, a liveness check, and stopped before the agent reports
data.why: 2026-09-30: six polling loops ran 5-21 hours after their agents had finished: they waited for EXIT=/FINISHED lines that reviews never wrote because the reviews hung (LAN Qwen), were cancelled, or had their output file overwritten in a shared scratchpad; one 'while pgrep -f "B-fix-declared-family-refute"' matched its own shell and could never end. data.summary: Under [enforce].commit_without_lease=block with the pre-commit framework, 'ddflow merge' (its merge commit in the PRIMARY checkout) is refused with 'You hold: (no live lease)' whenever the lease's events are not yet committed: pre-commit stashes unstaged files before running hooks, which reverts the primary's uncommitted .ddflow/events/<agent>.jsonl, so check-commit folds a log without the lease (and its heartbeats). Reproduced in run_nemo_run ONBOARDFIX.1 2026-10-01: refused twice with a live lease (1799 s left); the same check run outside git passed; committing the event log first, then 'ddflow merge', succeeded. ddflow merge also leaves the primary mid-merge (MERGE_HEAD) on that refusal. Fix options: read leases from a source pre-commit cannot stash (git-ignored lease file / index.db), or have merge commit the event log before the merge commit.

next --phase <id> silently returns 'Nothing actionable (0 ready, 0 running, 0 blocked)' when <id> is not an item at all (e.g. '159', whose tasks live under 159.A..159.I). Expected: an 'unknown phase' error (exit 1/2 with a message), or prefix-matching child phases. Repro on run_nemo_run: 'ddflow next --phase 159' -> empty, while 'ddflow show 159' -> 'no such item'. A driver reading the empty set as 'phase done' stops early (seen by the implement loop, 2026-10-01).

MCP ddflow_status has no size bound: on run_nemo_run (4831 tasks) it returns 721,813 chars / 18,351 lines (completed_tasks lists every done task), which exceeds the harness's tool-output limit and is spilled to a file. Brief has session.brief_max_tokens; status needs the same (summary counts + in-flight + ready by default, full lists behind a flag).

A lease expires silently while its holder waits on ddflow's OWN long commands: 'ddflow review <id>' (22-25 min on a LAN reasoning model) and 'ddflow gate run <id> unit_tests' (13 min) do not renew the lease of <id>, so the agent's next commit is refused by the commit_without_lease hook ('You hold: (no live lease)'). Seen on run_nemo_run 159.A.8, 2026-10-01. Expected: review / gate run / tests --item heartbeat the item they run for (they already know its id), or the refusal says the lease EXPIRED and that 'ddflow heartbeat <id>' renews it.

publish.yml mcp-registry job makes exactly one 'mcp-publisher publish' attempt, so a transient registry-side 504 (nginx 60s gateway timeout; upstream modelcontextprotocol/registry#1444, fix PR #1562 open: publish requests starve in the DB pool) fails the release and skips the tag job, though PyPI and both images shipped. Seen in publish #38 (0.1.6): manifest valid (PyPI README carries mcp-name, docker.io and ghcr.io images carry the io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name label, both resolve in ~1s), registry health 200, yet 504 after 60s and /v0.1/servers/io.github.delian%2Fddflow-mcp/versions/0.1.6 is 404 afterwards. Versions 0.1.4-0.1.6 are on PyPI and Docker with no git tag and no registry entry. Needs: retry with backoff, a check after each failure whether the version landed anyway (a 504 can hide a commit), and treating an already-published version as success.

MCP ddflow_merge fails its own commit_without_lease hook for an ADOPTED worktree: merge commits in the PRIMARY checkout, where the hook derives the agent id from the primary tree (Monster3-run_nemo_run-*), not the lease holder's (Monster3-bridge-cse_...-d42835). Output: every staged path '<-- held by 159.A.8 (<my id>)' yet 'You hold: (no live lease)', 'STOP: leased by ANOTHER agent', and the primary is LEFT MID-MERGE (MERGE_HEAD set, changes staged, 'Not committing merge') while the MCP result reports sha ''. Workaround: git merge --abort in the primary, then DDFLOW_AGENT=<holder> ddflow merge <id>. Fix: merge should run the commit with DDFLOW_AGENT=<the merging identity>, and abort its own merge on any failure (never leave the primary checkout mid-merge). Seen run_nemo_run 159.A.8, 2026-10-01.

review: default [[reviewer]].max_concurrency=4 is below chunks x hedge for any diff over ~2 chunks, so a review runs in WAVES and takes ~the sum of its slowest chunk per wave. Measured on run_nemo_run 2026-10-01 (LAN DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 5 chunks x hedge 2): 1301-1465 s at 4 vs 1122 s at max_concurrency=12 (one wave; floor = the runaway chunk's timeout). Suggest: default to chunks*hedge capped by a per-server limit, or warn when max_concurrency < chunks*hedge.

review: a chunk whose model exhausts max_tokens is reported 'unreachable: timed out' when timeout_s fires first (32000 tokens at <36 tok/s > 900 s), which reads as an endpoint problem. On run_nemo_run 159.A.8 the chunk DETERMINISTICALLY ran to max_tokens (5/5; finish_reason=length; low effort, thinking off, smaller chunks and a stop-rule prompt all failed) -- hedge copies only double the wasted compute. Suggest: label it 'did not converge (finish_reason=length / budget)', record tokens + finish_reason per chunk in evidence, and skip hedge retries of a chunk whose first copy hit length.

review: services.review.review() takes extra_rules and review_system.md renders a 'Project-specific rules' block, but no caller ever passes extra_rules (grep: only the parameter default) and no config key feeds it -- a dead knob; a project can only change reviewer instructions by overriding the whole template. Wire it from config (e.g. [review].extra_rules / a file path) or delete the parameter and the template block.

tests/test_api_layer.py::test_a_migrated_tool_reproduces_its_CLI_json_exactly[ddflow_companions] probes the real machine's companions twice (once per surface) and compares the results, so it fails whenever one probe is inconclusive and the other is not. Seen in the pre-push hook on main a91ac5c under -n 48: the CLI's 'npx --no-install @upstash/context7-mcp --help' exceeded DETECT_TIMEOUT_S (20s) -> state unknown, the MCP call's answered -> installed; push refused. data.body: Fixes bug B-flaky-companions-parity. The parametrised CLI-vs-MCP parity test runs 'companions list' on each surface; each probes the real companions (npx, docker, cargo tools) with a 20s timeout, so under load one probe times out (unknown) and the other answers (installed) and the comparison fails. Seed .ddflow/local/companion-probes.json with a fixed result for every companion id before either call: both surfaces read the cache, nothing shells out, and the comparison is of surfaces, not of two probes.
data.title: The companions surface-parity test seeds the probe cache instead of probing the machine twice (fixes bug B-flaky-companions-parity)

data.summary: gate run keeps only out[-2000:] plus a digest of output it then DISCARDS (services/gates.py ~976), so the digest can never be checked and anything before the last 2 KB is lost. For a gate command that reruns its failures (run_nemo_run's ddflow_test_gate.sh: parallel pass, then --lf serial rerun), the evidence shows only the rerun ('112 passed ... PASSED') and hides that the first pass had ~115 failures -- a red signal silently converted to a green record. Fix: write the full output to a per-run log (e.g. .ddflow/runs/<item>/<gate>-<ts>.log, git-ignored) and record its path next to the digest; optionally surface the gate's own summary lines (pytest '=== N failed' lines) from the whole output, not the tail.

data.claim: A stdlib TF-IDF cosine over FTS5 candidates finds the existing record in the top 3 for >=95% of real duplicates at a few ms per add; no score threshold can decide duplicate vs same-function-different-bug, so a human/agent answer is required.
data.falsifier: R@3 < 0.9 on the labelled set, or a threshold separating duplicates from hard negatives with precision >= 0.9 and recall >= 0.8.
data.mechanism: Duplicates share rare domain terms (event kinds, function names, flags); TF-IDF weights them; hard negatives share the same terms, so scores overlap.
data.probe: Benchmarked 13 matchers on 40 dup / 17 related / 18 hard-negative pairs + 98,345 negatives (ddflow log) and speed on run_nemo_run (6,100 records). TF-IDF+light stemmer: AP 0.537, R@1 0.68, R@3 0.95, R@5 0.975, lenient P 0.81 at 0.56; hard negatives 0.07-0.64; one same-root-cause pair at 0.14. FTS5 top-50 + rerank: 2.5/5.2 ms. rapidfuzz AP <= 0.29, MinHash 0.27, difflib 0.18, sklearn char TF-IDF 0.46 (203 MB), NLTK Porter 0.531 (no gain).
data.question: Can ddflow detect a duplicate bug/task/lesson at add time without an LLM, and which matcher?

data.alternatives: Warn-only (operator chose ask); reuse task.updated/bug.found for additions (loses simultaneous additions, overwrites bug summaries); close duplicates with a reason only (weakens the regression-test rule); add rapidfuzz/NLTK/scikit-learn (no accuracy gain, allowlist cost).
data.context: Research (2026-10-01, research R-dedupe-matchers): on 40 verified duplicate pairs, 17 related and 18 hard negatives from ddflow's own log, a stdlib TF-IDF cosine (code-aware tokenizer, ~10-line suffix stemmer, ids/shas masked) reranking FTS5 top-50 candidates puts the existing record in the top 3 for 95% (top 5 97.5%), finds the open task that fixes a new bug in the top 3 for 95%, at 2.5 ms median / 5.2 ms p95 per add on run_nemo_run's 6,100 records. NLTK, rapidfuzz, difflib, MinHash and scikit-learn were all no better or worse. A score cannot separate a duplicate from a different bug in the same function (hard negatives 0.43-0.64 sit inside the duplicate band), so ddflow shows candidates and the adding agent or operator answers. Benchmark scripts: the parent session's scratchpad dedup/ (corpus.py, labels.py, matchers.py, bench.py).
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-01: (1) on a match (score >= ask_threshold 0.55 with >= 8 content words, or the text names an existing id) an add is refused until answered new / extends X / duplicate of X / related X: interactive prompt on a TTY, exit 3 with ready commands for scripts, MCP re-call with relation=...; identical text (score 1.0) is recorded as a duplicate of the existing record without asking. Below the threshold candidates >= 0.35 are listed, never asked. (2) Additions and links are NEW event kinds (record.extended, link.recorded) plus link fields on add events; B168 (unknown kinds reported) lands first. extends/duplicate on an open unclaimed record appends to it verbatim with provenance; on a claimed, in-progress or closed record a new linked record is filed and the holder is told in brief. (3) A bug is closed as a duplicate only once X is fixed, citing X's regression test; nothing closes silently. (4) B198 is folded into this phase; B203 is a duplicate of B-semantic-recall. Defaults taken from the research recommendation (operator may revisit): no new runtime dependency (allowlist stays jinja2); every add kind is checked except session prompts and notes; thresholds 0.35 show / 0.55 ask; no LLM confirmation in this phase; the evaluation fixture is a redacted snapshot of real texts; search is within one project's log.
data.title: Every add checks for an existing record and asks; exact copies merge; additions are new event kinds; a duplicate bug closes only once its original is fixed

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-01, verbatim: "Add a feature development to ask agent to check if a bug, or feature for development, task, phase or whatever it adds, is not duplicated and if it is, to preferably update and extend the current content if it is not closed (in case of closed, or working on it - log a new bug, task, whatever, to not lose the changes) so the fix of the other bug to cover the new informantion of there is any. The idea is that we want to prevent duplication as much as possible (check if ddflow can by itself without llm - do a research for it maybe with nltk or other tools do a fuzzy search and ask the user in case of cli or agent to double check if the new data duplicates or extends pre existing one)? Add this as new phase for development with tasks after you do extensive research and propose a plan"

Research (2026-10-01, research R-dedupe-matchers): on 40 verified duplicate pairs, 17 related and 18 hard negatives from ddflow's own log, a stdlib TF-IDF cosine (code-aware tokenizer, ~10-line suffix stemmer, ids/shas masked) reranking FTS5 top-50 candidates puts the existing record in the top 3 for 95% (top 5 97.5%), finds the open task that fixes a new bug in the top 3 for 95%, at 2.5 ms median / 5.2 ms p95 per add on run_nemo_run's 6,100 records. NLTK, rapidfuzz, difflib, MinHash and scikit-learn were all no better or worse. A score cannot separate a duplicate from a different bug in the same function (hard negatives 0.43-0.64 sit inside the duplicate band), so ddflow shows candidates and the adding agent or operator answers. Benchmark scripts: the parent session's scratchpad dedup/ (corpus.py, labels.py, matchers.py, bench.py).

Decision D-no-duplicates (accepted). Task order: 1 -> 2 -> {3, 4 after B168} -> 5 -> {6, 7, 8, 9, 10} -> 11. Several tasks touch files bug-fix agents hold on 2026-10-01 (cli.py, mcp.py, api/knowledge.py, api/lifecycle.py, api/items.py, api/reporting.py, config.py): claim after those merge.
data.title: Nothing filed twice: every add checks for an existing record, extends it when it can, and links it when it cannot

data.summary: A claim refused for a glob overlap has no queue: waiting agents poll (ddflow wait / their own loops) and whoever polls first after a release takes the file, so a hot file such as ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py starves the longest waiter. Seen 2026-10-01: fix-review-pipeline (B-fix-review-rechunk, queued behind mcp.py from 20:42) was overtaken by later waiters five times (merge-report 19:41, setup-tree 20:03, sticky-binding 21:04, mcp-refusal-nulls 22:08, ...) and had waited over 2 h; holders kept the file for 40-65 min each because the lease spans slow reviews/roborev (6-25 min per shared-reviewer run) after the code edit is done. Expected: waiters registered by wait/claim are served FIFO (the next claim of a file offers it to the oldest waiter first), and/or a holder that is only waiting on a review can say so, so the file is released between edit and gates; doctor/brief should show 'N waiting on <file> since <time>' to the holder.

data.body: From the roborev speed research (2026-10-02; 126 jobs measured): a roborev job takes a median 299 s and p90 963 s, plus queue wait; an agent running 'roborev review --wait' holds its item's lease and file globs throughout (mcp.py was held 40-65 min per task). Design: 'ddflow gate run <id> standards --async' enqueues the job (roborev review <sha> without --wait), records the gate PENDING with the roborev job id, and returns at once; 'ddflow gate collect <id> standards' reads the job's STATUS (never the exit code: 'roborev review --wait -q' exits 1 for findings OR any failure) and records passed / failed(with findings) / unavailable (errored, canceled, timed out, no review stored). Merge and complete refuse while the gate is pending ('pending is not passed'). Leases renew while the item has pending jobs. Acceptance: pending is recorded with the job id and returns in < 5 s; a canceled, errored, timed-out or no-review job collects as unavailable, never passed; merge and complete refuse while pending; a regression test fails against the synchronous gate; CLI and MCP parity test. Reference: roborev wait --job N, roborev show --job N (a review stored after a wrapper timeout is still retrievable).
data.title: Async standards gate: gate run standards --async enqueues the roborev job and records pending; gate collect records the outcome

data.body: From the roborev speed research: agents ran 'timeout 600 roborev review <sha> --wait' and lost reviews (job 943 ran 27 min and stored its review; the 600 s wrapper lost it; 'roborev show --job 943' still had it) and jobs killed by the daemon's 30-minute timeout restart from scratch. Driver text: run 'roborev review <sha>' WITHOUT --wait, then 'roborev wait --job N' with ddflow heartbeats at least every 10 min; read the result with 'roborev show --job N' even after a timeout; never trust the exit code of 'roborev review --wait -q' (1 = findings OR any failure) - read the job status; review only the new tip (range jobs run 2.7x longer than single commits) unless a merge interaction is the point; do not hold file globs longer than the code edit needs. Acceptance: driver and every per-agent delta say so; the help-consistency test passes and every command named exists.
data.title: Driver docs: the standards gate enqueues roborev, waits by job id with heartbeats, and recovers a stored review with roborev show

data.body: From the roborev speed research (2026-10-02): since 14ca4ce (B-fix-reviewer-defaults) max_concurrency=0 sends every chunk x hedged copy at once, up to AUTO_CONCURRENCY_CEILING=32, and the shared reviewer endpoint was at 25-40 concurrent requests with per-stream speed falling from 65 to 51 tok/s; roborev is at most 4 of those. MEASURE FIRST: the same ddflow review of one fixed diff at ceilings 32 / 16 / 8 with roborev jobs running, recording both wall times. Lower the ceiling only if roborev's run time improves by more than ddflow review's slows; record the numbers as research. Never commit endpoint names. Acceptance: research record with the measurements; the ceiling constant and its test changed accordingly (or the task closed with the finding that 32 is right).
data.title: ddflow review's one-wave default sends at most 16 requests at once, not 32, once measured against roborev's run time

data.summary: gate record --model <author model> on a REVIEWER gate (rubber_duck/critic) overwrites the recorded reviewer's model, so reviewer independence is judged against the author's family and 'complete' refuses ('same family'); the --model option on gate record is documented for the reviewer model, while 'complete --model' is the author's. Seen by dedupe-t2-engine: recording with --model claude on a critic gate made it same-family; recording with --model deepseek fixed it. The two --model meanings should not share a spelling, or gate record should refuse an author-family model on a reviewer gate.

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-02: 'Make sure all new features or bug fixes are updating the README'. A task that adds or changes a command, flag, MCP tool, config knob, event kind, gate behaviour, default, refusal message or documented workflow, or fixes a bug whose behaviour the README describes, updates README.md IN THE SAME TASK (the section that describes it; a new section if none does). A change with no user- or agent-visible effect (pure refactor, test-only) records the reason when it skips (gate skip docs --reason ...). README.md is a [lease].shared_globs path: no claim on it is needed and none blocks; edits to different sections merge normally, a conflicting edit is resolved by rebasing onto main and keeping both. Counts the README quotes (knobs, sections, tools) must stay true: tests/test_log_read_cache.py pins some of them. Enforcement: a per-task docs check (task B-docs-per-task) reports a task that changed ddflow/** without touching README.md or recording a skip reason.

data.body: Decision D-readme-current. 75 merges landed on 2026-10-01 and README.md changed in only 9 commits. Audit: list every merge since 2026-10-01 (git log --merges), and for each decide whether it changed something README.md describes or should describe (commands, flags, MCP tools, config knobs, refusal behaviour, new workflows: resolve/rebind, review --chunk, review triage, shared_globs/append_only_globs, reviewer trust + reviewers approve, [dedupe], similar, merge keeping the worktree, etc.); update the README sections; keep quoted counts true (tests/test_log_read_cache.py). Acceptance: a table in the task report mapping each merge to its README section or 'no user-visible change'; every command/flag/tool named in the README exists (the help-consistency and remedy-text tests pass); no section contradicts the code.

data.body: Decision D-readme-current. Today the only docs gate is per phase (once, after the work is forgotten). Add a per-task check: at complete (and in gate status) compare the item's landed diff: if it changed ddflow/** (or the configured paths) and README.md is untouched, and no 'docs' outcome/skip with a reason is recorded, complete reports 'README not updated: record the section you changed, or gate skip docs --reason ...'. Decide in research whether this is a real gate in the task pipeline (new item in the default pipeline, evidence = the README diff, skip needs a reason) or a completion check with a configurable severity ([enforce].readme_with_code = off|warn|block, default warn); a gate is more visible, a check cheaper. Never block a test-only or docs-only change. Acceptance: a task that changes ddflow/** without README.md is reported; with a README change or a recorded skip reason it is not; test fails on main; the driver doc and the per-agent deltas say so.
data.title: Per-task docs check: a task that changed ddflow/** without touching README.md or recording a skip reason is reported before complete

data.claim: A mechanical report (referenced things exist, local links/anchors resolve, new public surface documented via configured extractors, opt-in counts, configured lint) attached as evidence to the existing docs gate catches real drift with tolerable noise, if scoped to an explicit doc allowlist.
data.falsifier: Precision below ~50% for identifier/link checks on real projects, or runtime beyond a few seconds.
data.mechanism: Drift is a diff between what docs name and what the code/tree contains; both are enumerable by stdlib scans at <2.5 s.
data.probe: Research (2026-10-02, R-docs-stage): measured on ddflow's, run_nemo_run's and home-simulator's own docs (read-only). Identifier/flag/tool references checked against tracked code: ~70-100% precise once history docs are excluded (ddflow: 2 real misses: `ddflow_research` should be ddflow_research_add, `ddflow setup` is the MCP tool not a CLI verb; run_nemo_run: 25 hits, several real). Path-like inline code: only 10-30% precise (runtime/generated paths, illustrative paths) -> notes only with an ignore list. Relative links/anchors (stdlib, <1 s): ~90% precise, real breakage found (run_nemo_run: 4 broken links, >=1 broken anchor; home-simulator: 1+1). Diff-vs-docs coverage via configured extractors replayed on ddflow since 10-01: 7 undocumented new flags/tools/knobs found (exactly what B-readme-catchup fixes). Counts need explicit markers (generic regex is noise). Age/co-change staleness is a prioritiser only (ARCHITECTURE.md: 557 code commits since last edit). No markdown linter is installed: lint must be a project-configured command, 'unavailable' when absent; ddflow adds no dependency.
data.question: Which mechanical checks can make ddflow's documentation stage guarantee a managed project's docs are current, in sync and clean?

data.alternatives: block by default (every false positive needs a skip); network link checks by default (CI flakiness); whole-tree docs checks (183 mostly-historical hits in home-simulator); mandatory docs gate (blocks projects with nothing worth checking); a generic README-count regex (noise).

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-docs-stage): (1) ddflow gains `ddflow docs check [--diff BASE]` (CLI + MCP) producing a deterministic report (referenced identifiers/flags/tools/paths exist, relative links and anchors resolve, new public surface undocumented via project-configured extractors, opt-in counts, configured lint command); the phase-level `docs` gate stays an agent gate but cannot be recorded passed without the report for the current tree (digest attached automatically); findings need a reason or a fix; a check that could not run is `unavailable`, never passed; skip stays allowed with a reason. (2) Severity default `warn` ([docs].severity warn|block|off). (3) Links: local only by default; `check_links = network` is opt-in and an unreachable network records unavailable. (4) Scope: an explicit allowlist [docs].check_paths (README plus named docs dirs), written by onboarding after asking the operator; whole-tree checking is not the default. (5) The docs gate is NOT made mandatory. (6) ddflow adds no dependency: lint/format run as a project-configured command ([docs].lint_command), unavailable when the binary is missing. (7) The commit hook keeps docsync (removed names); it is not extended. The per-task step is B-docs-per-task and the README catch-up B-readme-catchup (D-readme-current), driver drift B-fix-driver-drift: this phase builds on them.

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-upstream-reporting): (1) ddflow gains `ddflow bug report` (CLI + MCP `ddflow_bug_report`) and a bug `scope` (project|ddflow); when ddflow or an agent finds/suspects a defect in ddflow itself the operator is PROPOSED an upstream report. (2) Default [upstream].mode = propose (off|propose); NO automatic reporting in v1, not even for mechanical detectors; only the operator can set the mode (an agent's ddflow_configure cannot raise it). (3) The bundle is built by ddflow from allowlisted fields (ddflow version, install kind, commit, python/os, redacted command/exit/traceback with ddflow-relative frames, allowlisted knobs, a minimal aliased log excerpt, provenance) — the agent supplies only a short title and 'what I expected', redacted the same way. NEVER sent: secrets, private IPs/hostnames, home/repo paths, emails, project and repo names, file contents/diffs, operator prompts, item titles/bodies, reviewer endpoints ([upstream].redact_extra adds the operator's own terms). (4) Delivery shipped in v1: a local file (.ddflow/local/reports/), a prefilled GitHub issue URL, AND `gh issue create -R <repo>` when gh is installed and authenticated (unavailable, never silent, otherwise); the REST-with-token and connector routes are later. (5) Who may send: BOTH the CLI (interactive prompt at a terminal) and MCP are possible, MCP being the default surface; consent is always an operator-held credential bound to the digest of the exact rendered text: at a terminal the interactive yes, over MCP a one-time token the operator mints at the terminal (`ddflow bug report approve <id>`) and gives the agent; an agent-supplied 'confirm=true' is NEVER consent; any edit after the yes invalidates it; per submission, never per session. (6) Fix proposals: when the agent has ddflow's source (own dev tree or a configured [upstream].source), the fix is made on a branch with a failing-first regression test through ddflow's normal gates and delivered as a `git format-patch` file in .ddflow/local/reports/; ddflow NEVER pushes or opens a PR; a fork PR would need its own explicit per-submission yes in a later decision. (7) The dev tree itself: bugs stay in the local queue; the upstream mirror is optional. (8) Records `bug.reported_upstream` (url, number, delivery, time, digest) close the loop later.

The same crash class probably exists in every add renderer (lesson/research/memory/bug/task/phase): each prints fields the refusal does not carry. Interim: the B-dedupe-default-warn hotfix stops refusals; the real fix belongs with B-add-dedupe-surfaces (render a refusal with its candidates and the --new/--extends/--duplicate-of/--related options), plus a test that every add command renders a refusal without a traceback.

chunk_findings.detail: Private IPv4 addresses written with leading zeros are not redacted. `_is_private` calls `ipaddress.IPv4Address(raw)`, but Python’s `ipaddress` module rejects zero-padded octets with `ValueError`. The `except ValueError` returns `False`, so the `keep` predicate returns `True` and the match is left unchanged. For example, `redact_report("connect to 172.16.001.1")` returns the string with `172.16.001.1` still present; the acceptance criterion that no 172.16–31.x address remains is violated. The same happens for `010.0.0.1`, `192.168.001.1`, etc. The `private_addresses` helper inherits the same blind spot.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/redact_report.py (the `_is_private`/IPv4 redaction path)

chunk_findings.detail: The change description states the redaction must remove "private IPv4/IPv6 and `.lan`/`.local`/`.internal`/`home.arpa` hosts", and the test module's own fixture relies on `.local` being redacted (`printer." + "local`, enforced only by `out.counts["host"] == 4`). However `_leaks`, the leak detector used by the main acceptance test `test_every_bug_summary_and_rendering_is_clean`, matches only `lan|internal|home\.arpa` and omits `local`. Since the synthetic test's `.local` coverage comes from a hardcoded `counts["host"] == 4`, the corpus loop over real `bug.found` summaries has no `.local` detector at all. Concrete failure: a real event whose `data.summary` contains e.g. `nas.local` will, if `redact_report` regresses and leaves it visible, still produce `_leaks(out.text) == []` (the hostname check uses only `host`, the `.lan` regex ignores `.local`, and `_corpus_projects` only matches `src|git|code|work|projects` path segments), so `assert not left` passes and the `.local` host leaks out undetected by the very test that is supposed to guarantee "no ... .local ... leaves in a report". The other three suffixes from the stated detector list are present in the same alternation, which indicates `local` was dropped from the list rather than deliberately excluded.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_report.py `_leaks` (host check, `r"\b[\w-]+\.(?:lan|internal|home\.arpa)\b"`)

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-02: can the version live in one place instead of ddflow/__init__.py, ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py (SERVER_INFO), pyproject.toml and server.json (version, the pypi package version, two OCI identifier tags) -- plus uv.lock, which records the project's own version and is re-locked on every bump. Investigated (see the scratch probe): with hatchling,  and  the wheel/sdist take the version from __init__.py (verified: a scratch project built demo_mcp-0.1.10 after editing only __init__.py), AND uv.lock then carries NO version for the project, so a bump no longer touches uv.lock (verified:  passes after the version changes). Runtime reads it by plain import (no importlib.metadata: stale in editable/PYTHONPATH source runs, which ddflow's hook script and worktrees use). Design: (1) single literal  in ddflow/__init__.py; (2) pyproject.toml dynamic version; (3) mcp.py SERVER_INFO built from __version__; (4) server.json becomes a generated, committed artifact: a template server.template.json with a version placeholder (also in the OCI identifier tags and the pypi package version; OCI packages carry NO version field, see B-fix-registry-oci-version) rendered by scripts/render_server_json.py (stdlib; a --check mode); CI renders it in / before publish and a test fails if the committed file differs from the render; (5) scripts/bump.sh edits only __init__.py then renders server.json (no uv re-lock); (6) every place that greps pyproject.toml for  (publish.yml gate/pypi jobs, release.sh, bump.sh, tests/test_packaging.py::test_the_declared_versions_agree) reads __init__.py instead; (7) the primary .venv editable metadata is stale until a reinstall -- code must not depend on it. Rejected: hatch-vcs / git-tag versions (CI bumps by commit and creates the tag AFTER publishing); importlib.metadata at runtime (stale in source trees); making pyproject the single source (it is not shipped in the wheel, so a runtime read needs two code paths). Acceptance (failing-first): after editing ONLY ddflow/__init__.py and running render_server_json.py,  yields that version, ddflow 0.1.9 and the MCP serverInfo agree, server.json carries it in version, the pypi package and both OCI tags,  passes, and tests/test_packaging.py holds; a test fails when server.json is not the render of the template; the publish workflow's version steps read __init__.py (actionlint clean); README Cutting-a-release section updated (D-readme-current).
data.title: One place declares the version: ddflow/__init__.py; pyproject.toml reads it (hatch dynamic), mcp.py imports it, server.json is rendered from a template, uv.lock stops recording it

data.body:
Operator question 2026-10-02: can the version live in one place instead of ddflow/__init__.py, ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py (SERVER_INFO), pyproject.toml and server.json (version, the pypi package version, two OCI identifier tags) -- plus uv.lock, which records the project's own version and is re-locked on every bump.

Investigated with a scratch project (read-only probe): with hatchling, `dynamic = ["version"]` and `[tool.hatch.version] path = "ddflow/__init__.py"`, the wheel and sdist take the version from __init__.py (a scratch project built demo_mcp-0.1.10 after editing only __init__.py), AND uv.lock then carries NO version for the project, so a bump no longer touches uv.lock (`uv lock --check` passes after the version changes). Runtime reads it by plain import (no importlib.metadata: stale in editable / PYTHONPATH source runs, which ddflow's hook script and worktrees use).

Design: (1) a single literal __version__ in ddflow/__init__.py; (2) pyproject.toml dynamic version; (3) mcp.py SERVER_INFO built from __version__; (4) server.json becomes a generated, committed artifact: a template server.template.json with a version placeholder (also in the OCI identifier tags and the pypi package version; OCI packages carry NO version field, see B-fix-registry-oci-version) rendered by scripts/render_server_json.py (stdlib; a --check mode); CI renders it in the gate/verify jobs before publish and a test fails if the committed file differs from the render; (5) scripts/bump.sh edits only __init__.py then renders server.json (no uv re-lock); (6) every place that greps pyproject.toml for the version line (publish.yml gate and pypi jobs, release.sh, bump.sh, tests/test_packaging.py::test_the_declared_versions_agree) reads __init__.py instead; (7) the primary .venv editable metadata is stale until a reinstall -- code must not depend on it.

Rejected: hatch-vcs / git-tag versions (CI bumps by commit and creates the tag AFTER publishing); importlib.metadata at runtime (stale in source trees); making pyproject the single source (it is not shipped in the wheel, so a runtime read needs two code paths).

Acceptance (failing-first): after editing ONLY ddflow/__init__.py and running render_server_json.py, `uv build` yields that version, `ddflow --version` and the MCP serverInfo agree, server.json carries it in version, the pypi package and both OCI tags, `uv lock --check` passes, and tests/test_packaging.py holds; a test fails when server.json is not the render of the template; the publish workflow's version steps read __init__.py (actionlint clean); README "Cutting a release" section updated (D-readme-current).

data.probe: Research (2026-10-02, R-extres-evaluation) of an externally produced 'DDFlow MCP Extension Research' document against ddflow main. Verdict: a generic survey written from three Glama tool pages; ~2/3 of its proposals already exist in stronger form, ~1/4 conflict with ddflow's design (remote multi-tenant server, SSE/event bus, background LLM consolidation, tree-sitter/LSP/sqlite-vec/ONNX against the dependency allowlist, per-step full suite against the operator's batch-integration request); its load-bearing numbers (60-95% from tool consolidation, 70-85% from Markdown) rest on vendor/forum posts and could not be verified. Real gaps, MEASURED: (1) tools/list is 90 tools, 119 KB (~30k tokens) + 12 KB handshake text; the as_agent description repeats on 89 tools = 27 KB (22.7%); merging tools would save only ~5%; a 28-tool core set is 44 KB; (2) MCP read payloads are 28-35x their prose rendering: next 35 KB vs 1.2 KB CLI text, show 11 KB vs 1 KB, recall 32 KB, decision_list 40 KB, progress 150 KB; compact JSON alone saves only 10-37%; (3) no untrusted-data fencing or provenance: channels are PR-added event-log lines (merge=union, no signatures), imported ADRs becoming accepted decisions, agent-written records re-injected, PR review text, the reviewer diff in a single fence; (4) no model-tier hint on tasks; (5) no detector for the same gate failing the same way repeatedly; (6) ddflow_configure can set a non-human gate command to 'true' locally.

data.title: A lean MCP surface and trusted context: smaller tool list and payloads, provenance and fencing, tiers, a model-tier hint, a repeated-failure detector

data.body:
Measured (R-extres-evaluation): tools/list = 90 tools, 119,169 bytes compact (~30k tokens); the as_agent description repeats on 89 tools = ~27 KB (22.7%), injected in one place in mcp.py (_schema/_properties, near line 2535); relation + check_only repeat on 7 add tools = ~5 KB; the five longest tools (decision_add, lesson_add, task_add, research_add, phase_add) are 2.5-3.2 KB each. Shorten the shared descriptions (full text lives once, e.g. in ddflow_help and the handshake instructions), trim long descriptions without dropping a rule an agent needs (tests pin several: run the whole suite), keep every tool name and parameter (parity ratchets in tests/test_mcp_parity.py unchanged). Acceptance (failing-first): a ratchet test fails if the compact tools/list exceeds a budget (set at the measured result + small slack) or the as_agent description is repeated in full on more than one tool; before/after bytes recorded in the task report; target <= ~92 KB. B-split-mcp-tools also holds mcp.py: coordinate, claim only when ready to edit.

Phase B-lean-and-trusted; decision D-lean-and-trusted; research R-extres-evaluation.
data.title: Trim the MCP tool list: one short shared as_agent/relation/check_only description and tighter long descriptions, no tool renamed, with a byte budget ratchet

data.body:
Measured over the real MCP path: next 35,189 B (CLI text 1,248 B; 26 KB is the blocked list), show 11,412 B (CLI text 988 B; gates 6.9 KB), recall 32,454 B (seven kinds, whole records), decision_list 39,948 B, progress 149,575 B, status 15,697 B (bounded to 25/list since B-fix-status-bound) while the CLI --json is 62 KB; MCP pretty-prints every JSON body with indent=2 (mcp.py ~2756). Compact separators + null/empty stripping alone save only 10-37%; projection and bounding win by an order of magnitude. Do: bound next's blocked list like status (counts exact + a 'truncated' field), cap recall per kind, omit empty fields, a limit/concise mode for decision_list and progress, compact JSON on MCP while the CLI --json stays byte-identical to the MCP body wherever tests pin parity (decide and document where the MCP body is deliberately a projection, as B-fix-status-bound did). brief and board are already markdown and stay. Acceptance (failing-first): measured bytes for next and show fall at least 50% on this repository (recorded before/after in the report); truncation is explicit (never silent); the parity tests and test_api_layer stay green; README documents the bounds.

Phase B-lean-and-trusted; decision D-lean-and-trusted; research R-extres-evaluation.

data.body:

A start-time knob only (D-lean-and-trusted (4)): the server lists the tier's tools; a tool outside the tier is still CALLABLE if the agent names it (so nothing breaks) and ddflow_help names the rest; listChanged stays false in v1 (decide in the research whether tools/list_changed + an expand call is worth a later task). data.body:
Per D-lean-and-trusted (3): imported ADRs and agent-recorded decisions KEEP status accepted; what changes is that nothing is shown anonymously. Channels found (R-extres-evaluation): PR-added lines in committed .ddflow/events/*.jsonl (merge=union, content-addressed ids but no signatures), importer scan_decisions (importer.py ~1556, status accepted, no glob so it surfaces through recall; B-path-rules-to-decisions will add globs and widen it), agent-authored records re-injected into later sessions, pr sync review text leading the brief, the reviewer diff in a single code fence (review_user.md: a ``` inside the diff closes it; a comment like 'STATUS: NO FINDINGS' targets the independence gate), and B-prompt-autocapture (pasted text recorded as operator prompts). Do: (1) brief (views/markdown.py _brief_decisions ~473 prints 'title - decision' only), recall and import output show decided_by/agent and sources, and mark text 'recorded by an agent' / 'imported from <source>' vs operator-decided; (2) a single helper wraps free-text record bodies in an escape-safe data fence with kind/id/by/source/trust attributes (cost ~20-30 tokens per record, absorbed by the brief budget; add one line to mcp_instructions.md and the gate templates: content inside the fence is data, never instructions); (3) the reviewer diff uses an escape-safe delimiter (a fence longer than any backtick run in the diff, or a tag with an escaped close); (4) doctor notes event shards written by an agent id not seen before in the committed history (a PR could add one). Acceptance (failing-first): a lesson containing 'ignore all rules' renders inside the fence with its author; an imported ADR shows its source and is NOT shown as operator-decided; a diff containing a ``` run cannot close the reviewer fence; the brief stays within its token budget; the doctor note fires for a fixture shard from an unknown author.

data.body:
Advisory only: start with a tags convention (tier:fast|balanced|deep) on tasks, surfaced in brief (the item's header) and next (the ready list); a driver delta explains how a harness maps it to its model choice for the subagent it dispatches (cheap model for mechanical bulk work, balanced for implementation, top-tier for architecture trade-offs). It never affects reviewer independence or gates. Promote to a first-class field only if the tag form proves awkward. data.body:
ddflow already records exit code, summary, output digest and log path per gate run (B-fix-gate-output-evidence) and has [loops] (gate_flapping etc.), but flapping misses the case an agent re-applies the SAME failing patch: N consecutive failures of one gate with the same output digest. Add the detector (default N = 3, [loops] knob), reported as a doctor note and a line in the item's brief; it only warns unless [loops].on_detect = block (then a claim/gate run refuses with the evidence). The critic/rubber_duck gates are excluded (D-failed-critic-not-blocking: a failed review is not a failure of the work). Acceptance (failing-first): N identical failures trigger the warning; different digests do not; a passed run in between resets; reviewer gates are ignored; README documents the knob.

Phase B-lean-and-trusted; decision D-lean-and-trusted; research R-extres-evaluation.

data.summary: The ddflow_loops MCP tool description in ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py still lists only the old loop detectors; it does not mention the new repeated_failure detector (one gate failing N times in a row with an identical output digest, [loops].max_repeated_failures, default 3), so an agent reading tools/list does not learn it exists. data.decision: Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-export): (1) `ddflow export <doc>` (CLI) and `ddflow_export` (MCP) generate documents from the event log: roadmap, bugs, rules, status, worklog, sessions, decisions index, changelog (and release notes for a version); printing to stdout is the default (review on demand, with --since/--version/--phase/--status/--limit, a size cap with an explicit truncation footer, --diff); writing needs --out/--update (CLI, interactive confirm on a TTY) or write=true plus a repo-relative path (MCP). All document tasks ship together (operator: all at once). (2) Default targets are at the REPO ROOT (ROADMAP.md, BUGS.md, RULES.md, STATUS.md, LOG.md, SESSION.md, CHANGELOG.md, DECISIONS.md), committed like any file; because they are not self-managed paths, every export target is registered as a [lease].shared_globs (generated) or append_only_globs (append mode) path automatically so no claim on them is needed; [export.<doc>].path overrides. (3) Update modes: whole generated file with a header carrying doc kind, ddflow version and a digest of the BODY (hand-edit detection; `--check` regenerates and compares exactly; no log digest); marker regions (<!-- ddflow:begin NAME --> ... <!-- ddflow:end NAME -->) inside hand-written files; append-only logs after the last exported event id. A hand-edited generated file or an unmarked file is never overwritten without --force. Writes are atomic under a lock. Paths outside the repo, symlinks, .git and .ddflow are refused. (4) Changelog: derive first (explicit field, then Conventional Commit prefix, then tags, then the 'fixes bug' title suffix, else Changed) with ONE optional field `changelog {category, line, skip}` set by `ddflow complete --changelog "Added: ..."`; `complete` never prompts and never requires it; the version of an item comes from git (merged_sha ancestor of the tag and not of the previous tag), nothing is reconstructed before the first tag. B167 is superseded; B174 narrows to version-file bumping; B202(b) becomes the export kind digest. (5) Safety: [export].redact is ON by default for every target (they are public-repo documents at the root), using services/redact_report.py, with 'redacted: N' in the header; free text from agents is fenced when served over MCP (reuse B-security-provenance's core/provenance.py, do not duplicate); replay is not an export kind. (6) Refresh: export may be refreshed automatically after merge or at phase close when the operator enables it ([export].refresh = off|merge|phase_close, default off; also expressible as a [cadence] entry); never without being enabled. (7) 'Rules' = decisions in force (by governing path) + lessons + the enforced workflow settings; imported rulebooks are not exported. (8) No new dependency (Jinja2 is already allowed); new optional event fields and the [export] section follow the forward-compat rule (B1c4a2346a9). run_nemo_run's frozen-file hooks stay the project's own decision (not touched here).

A registry of document kinds {name, default_target, filters, update_mode, renderer}; pure (state, events, filters) -> data functions per kind (Python), presentation in Jinja2 templates ddflow/templates/export/<kind>.md.j2 resolved like prompts (services/prompts.py: [export.<name>].template, then .ddflow/templates/export/, then shipped; StrictUndefined); a single-pass parent->children index (the naive phase->tasks lookup took 6.6 s on 5,632 items; test 5,632 items under 100 ms); header '<!-- ddflow:generated doc=<kind> v=<ddflow version> body-sha256=<12 hex> -->' + 'Generated by ddflow from the event log - edit the source, not this file' (digest of the rendered BODY only, never the log); stable sort keys with an id tie-break, no wall clock in the body; stdout rendering with --max-bytes (default 60,000) and an explicit '[truncated: N more; use --since/--limit]' footer. data.body:
Per D-export (3). Whole file: header digest; --check exits 0 fresh / 1 stale or hand-edited / 2 could not run; hand-edit detection by sha256(body) != header digest -> refuse without --force and show the diff; an existing file with no ddflow header or marker is never overwritten without --force. Marker regions: replace only the region body, keep surrounding prose byte for byte; missing, duplicate or unbalanced markers refuse. Append-only: append entries after the last exported event id recorded in the header; never rewrite old lines; registers the target in append_only_globs. Path safety: refuse paths outside the repo, symlinks (including a symlinked parent), .git/, .ddflow/, absolute paths. Atomic write under the same lock as the hand-edit check (infra/tomlcfg atomic_write/locked). data.decision: Operator 2026-10-02: it must be possible for the user to specify WHICH documents are generated, IF ANY, and to generate them on demand by asking the MCP, with the CLI, or as part of the phase document sync. data.decision: Operator 2026-10-02 (refines D-export): the FORMAT of every exported document is owned by ddflow and defined by a Jinja2 template per document kind; the agent supplies no formatting (this also holds when ddflow runs as a remote or containerised MCP server: the server renders from the repository's data and templates, the client only receives or requests the result). (1) Every kind has a shipped default template ddflow/templates/export/<kind>.md.j2; resolution order: [export.<doc>].template (a path), then .ddflow/templates/export/<kind>.md.j2 in the project, then the shipped default - the same resolution as prompts (services/prompts.py). (2) `ddflow export eject <doc>` copies the shipped template into .ddflow/templates/export/ for editing (like `prompts eject`); `ddflow export <doc> --template PATH` renders once with an ad hoc template for review; `ddflow export validate [<doc>]` renders every selected document against the current data and reports template errors with file and line. (3) Query/grouping/filtering stays in Python (a pure (state, events, filters) -> data function per kind); the template receives ONLY that plain data (dicts, lists, strings, numbers) plus a small set of documented filters/helpers (e.g. md_escape, wrap, date, truncate, bar); it receives no objects with methods, no repo handle, no file or process access. (4) Templates are rendered in a Jinja2 SANDBOX (jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment, StrictUndefined, no autoescape) because a template may come from a cloned repository: a template cannot reach Python internals, read files or run commands; a template that raises or times out is reported as a template error (exit 2 'could not run'), never as an empty clean document and never partially written. (5) The data contract per kind (the variable names, types and ordering) is documented in the README/help and carries a `schema_version` that the template can check; ddflow changes it compatibly (add fields, never rename or remove within a major) and notes changes in the release notes; the shipped templates are regression-tested against golden output. (6) A user override stays deterministic: same data + same template -> same bytes. The header (ddflow:generated marker + body digest) is added by ddflow around the template's body, not by the template, so a user template cannot remove hand-edit protection. (7) A ddflow upgrade never overwrites an ejected template: `ddflow export validate` and doctor note when the shipped default for a kind is newer than the ejected copy (compare a recorded shipped-template digest), like the driver-docs drift note.

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-task-time): the review budget is part of ddflow's workflow, not agent-instruction prose. (1) [review].max_rounds (default 2; 0 = unlimited) bounds FULL review rounds per gate per item; counted from the gate's review records on the item; starting another full round beyond the budget is refused with exit 3 naming the alternatives (a delta review of the fix commits, `ddflow review triage` of the remaining findings, --force --reason); [review].on_exceed = refuse|warn (default refuse for full rounds; a delta review and triage are never refused). (2) A review of a gate that already has a recorded review defaults to a DELTA of the commits since the last reviewed head (evidence records the reviewed head), merging coverage into the gate record like --chunk does; `--full` forces a full round (counts against the budget). (3) `ddflow review <id> --gate rubber_duck,critic` (or --gate all) runs the reviewer gates concurrently (CLI and MCP), because they review the same diff. (4) Convergence is shown: `gate status` and `brief` say 'critic round 2/2, findings: N untriaged, M confirmed HIGH/MEDIUM' and 'review converged: yes/no' (yes = every finding triaged and no confirmed HIGH/MEDIUM defect left); `complete`/merge print a NOTE when not converged and never block (D-failed-critic-not-blocking stands). (5) [review].time_budget_s (default 900) bounds one review run: chunks not reviewed in time make the run `partial` with what was reviewed, never a hang. (6) Lease hold visibility: while an item holds contended globs (other agents waiting, claim-fairness registry) and is only running review gates, brief and doctor say so with the hold time and [lease].hold_warn_s (default 1800) warns the holder; a warning, never an eviction. (7) The shared agent-instruction text on review rounds is replaced by the shipped driver docs describing these features. Defaults are revisitable; none of it blocks completion.
data.title: The review budget is a ddflow workflow feature, configurable and enforced: bounded full rounds, delta re-reviews by default, parallel reviewer gates, convergence shown, hold time visible

data.body:
Per D-review-budget (1). Count full rounds from the gate's recorded review records on the item (evidence already carries diff_sha/coverage since B-fix-review-rechunk; add a round number and a full/delta flag); [review].max_rounds default 2 (0 = unlimited), [review].on_exceed refuse|warn default refuse; the refusal (exit 3) names the alternatives: `ddflow review <id> --gate G --delta`, `ddflow review triage ...`, `--force --reason "..."`; a delta review and a triage are never refused; --force is recorded. Acceptance (failing-first): the third full round on a gate is refused with the alternatives; delta and triage still work; warn mode only warns; max_rounds = 0 never refuses; the count survives a re-claim; knob documented in README and config --explain, forward-compat for unknown knobs.

data.title: [review].max_rounds and on_exceed: bound full review rounds per gate per item, with the round counter in the evidence

data.body:
Per D-review-budget (2). The evidence records the reviewed head (and the diff base); a later `ddflow review <id> --gate G` reviews only base..HEAD of the new commits (the existing --base/--commit machinery), merges the delta's findings and coverage into the gate record (like --chunk's merge) and carries earlier triage over only for byte-identical findings; --full forces a full round (counts against max_rounds); the output says 'delta review of N commits since <sha>' so nobody mistakes it for a full pass; the gate status shows full rounds and delta rounds separately. If the base head is not an ancestor of HEAD (rebased) it falls back to a full round and says why. Acceptance (failing-first): after a first review a one-commit fix is reviewed as a delta (diff chars = the fix, not the whole diff); --full is a full round; a rebase falls back; triage carry-over rules; MCP parity; the tools/list budget stays green.

data.body:
Operator idea 2026-10-02: hold hot-file leases only for edit and merge, while reviews run on the committed branch. It needs care: if the holder releases the globs before its branch merges, another agent can edit the same files and the two merges conflict (or silently combine wrongly). RESEARCH FIRST (record it): measure how often two agents' unmerged branches touch the same file today (git log across today's worktree branches: how many pairs conflicted on merge? the stale-rules/merge-main-in cost), what the claim model records (lease globs vs item globs, B-fix-claim-globs), and design options: (a) a 'review phase' lease state: the item keeps its claim on the ITEM and its worktree but its globs convert from exclusive to a 'pending merge' reservation that lets another agent claim an overlapping item only if it first rebases on the holder's branch (ddflow merges the first branch to main as soon as it is ready; the second agent starts from main); (b) split the lease into edit-lease (exclusive, short) and merge-queue entry (ordered); (c) automatic rebase of the second branch onto main when the first merges, with conflict surfacing. Recommend one, with the conflict rate measured, the failure modes (silent semantic conflicts), and the operator decisions needed; implement only after the operator confirms the design (propose it with a decision, leave the task blocked). Acceptance of the research: a report with measured conflict frequency and a recommended design; a failing-first test list for the implementation.

Phase B-hot-files; research R-task-time (hot-file hold times).

data.summary: Reported by lean3-tool-tiers (B-mcp-tool-tiers): the --globs flag on 'ddflow claim' was ignored for that claim (it had to widen the lease afterwards with 'ddflow update --globs' to add the instructions template, the parity test and tests/conftest.py). B-fix-claim-globs (69a589b) and B-fix-globs-surfaces (2a19725) were meant to make claim --globs repeatable and recorded on both lease and item; this is either a regression (e.g. claim fairness / refused-then-retried claim path), a CLI-vs-MCP difference (the agent may have claimed over MCP, where globs come from the item), or the agent's misuse. Reproduce first: claim an item with a --globs value that differs from the item's stored globs, from the CLI and over MCP, and show the recorded lease globs; close as invalid with the probe if it works.

ddflow review sends untracked worktree files in its prompt ('main..HEAD + working tree'), so a draft file an agent left untracked in its worktree is reviewed as part of the diff and findings can be about files that are not in the commit (seen by exp1-core-write on B-export-core). Expected: the review diff is exactly the branch commits (or committed + tracked-modified), with untracked files excluded or listed separately as 'untracked, not reviewed'.

roborev review HEAD run from an item's worktree once enqueued the PRIMARY checkout's HEAD (main) instead of the worktree branch's HEAD, so the standards gate was recorded against the wrong commit (seen by exp1-core-write; passing the explicit sha worked). roborev resolves the repo from the shared git dir; the agent instructions and the standards gate prompt should pass an explicit sha (roborev review <sha>), and ddflow's standards gate evidence should record which sha was reviewed and refuse when it differs from the item's branch head.

The export core's shared md_escape filter escapes every underscore, so identifiers in generated documents render as run\_nemo\_run / B\-export\-core style noise in the source text (seen in the RULES.md export). CommonMark does not treat intraword underscores as emphasis, and identifiers are normally wrapped in code spans: md_escape should escape only what would change rendering (leading/trailing emphasis markers, line-start list/heading markers, pipes in tables, backslashes, html-looking angle brackets) and leave intraword underscores alone. Reported by exp5-rules; golden tests of the shipped templates must be updated with the fix.

data.body: Operator 2026-10-02: 'Add a feature when ddflow record session to preserve it even without a session id, using the latest session id. In fact every prompt should have session id even if it is implicit.' Today `ddflow session prompt <session-id> --text` refuses without a session id (the first argument is read as the id) and a note/prompt with no session is lost. Make the session id optional on session prompt and session note (CLI and MCP session_prompt/session_note): resolve it as the explicit id, else the harness session id the autocapture hook keys on (B-prompt-autocapture), else the latest OPEN session for this agent/worktree, else open an implicit session (marked implicit in its start event) and use that. Never refuse and never drop text because the id is missing. Every session.prompt/session.note event then carries a session id, including prompts from the autocapture hook when the harness gives none. Say which session was used in the output ('recorded in session S (latest)' / '(implicit, new)') so nobody mistakes it. Ambiguity rule: several open sessions -> the most recent by last event; an ended session is never reused. Backfill: `ddflow doctor` notes existing prompt/note events with no session id and `ddflow session adopt-orphans` (or doctor --fix) attaches them to the nearest session by time. Acceptance (failing-first): prompt with no id lands in the latest open session; with no open session an implicit one is created and the text kept; explicit id unchanged; ended session not reused; redaction still applied before disk; MCP parity; README session section updated (D-readme-current); tools/list byte budget stays green.

Per D-review-budget (1). Count full rounds from the gate's recorded review records on the item (evidence already carries diff_sha/coverage since B-fix-review-rechunk; add a round number and a full/delta flag); [review].max_rounds default 2 (0 = unlimited), [review].on_exceed refuse|warn default refuse; the refusal (exit 3) names the alternatives: `ddflow review <id> --gate G --delta`, `ddflow review triage ...`, `--force --reason "..."`; a delta review and a triage are never refused; --force is recorded. Acceptance (failing-first): the third full round on a gate is refused with the alternatives; delta and triage still work; warn mode only warns; max_rounds = 0 never refuses; the count survives a re-claim; knob documented in README and config --explain, forward-compat for unknown knobs.

Phase B-review-budget; decision D-review-budget; research R-task-time.

OPERATOR 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Do this but not only for this project but also a default for all projects, however make it user or mcp configurable so the user could change it in case of need. A cap of 2 full review rounds, then triage.' => The cap is a SHIPPED DEFAULT for every project (the dataclass default in config.py, not a value written into this repository's config.toml): [review].max_rounds = 2, [review].on_exceed = refuse. It must be changeable by the user at every layer: the shared .ddflow/config.toml, the machine-local .ddflow/local/config.toml (`ddflow config --local`), the env override, the CLI (`ddflow config review.max_rounds 0 [--local]`), and MCP (`ddflow_configure` must accept review.max_rounds and review.on_exceed, including on the local layer; agents may NOT raise or disable it for an item without the operator: a per-item --force --reason is the recorded exception, and changing the knob over MCP is reported to the operator). `max_rounds = 0` = unlimited, `on_exceed = warn` = warn only. The refusal message names how to change it. After the cap, a delta recheck of the fix commits and `ddflow review triage` stay ALWAYS allowed (so the later-round findings are not simply lost). README and config --explain document the default and how to change it (D-readme-current).

Per D-review-budget (2). The evidence records the reviewed head (and the diff base); a later `ddflow review <id> --gate G` reviews only base..HEAD of the new commits (the existing --base/--commit machinery), merges the delta's findings and coverage into the gate record (like --chunk's merge) and carries earlier triage over only for byte-identical findings; --full forces a full round (counts against max_rounds); the output says 'delta review of N commits since <sha>' so nobody mistakes it for a full pass; the gate status shows full rounds and delta rounds separately. If the base head is not an ancestor of HEAD (rebased) it falls back to a full round and says why. Acceptance (failing-first): after a first review a one-commit fix is reviewed as a delta (diff chars = the fix, not the whole diff); --full is a full round; a rebase falls back; triage carry-over rules; MCP parity; the tools/list budget stays green.

Phase B-review-budget; decision D-review-budget; research R-task-time.

OPERATOR 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Make sure this is done again for this project but by default for all ddflow projects too, but make sure user or mcp can configure this behavior in case of change needed: Land delta re-reviews first (B-review-delta-default), which the agent estimates saves about 150 to 200 min per day.'. => Knob [review].delta_default (default true; false = every review is a full round, the old behaviour); --full always forces a full round. LAND THIS BEFORE the other review-budget tasks that can: it depends only on the round/full-delta evidence flag from B-review-budget-rounds (in flight, agent rb-rounds) — coordinate with that agent's evidence field names rather than inventing a second one. The behaviour is a SHIPPED DEFAULT for every project (config dataclass default, not a value in this repository's config.toml) and is changeable at every layer: shared .ddflow/config.toml, machine-local .ddflow/local/config.toml (`ddflow config --local`), env override, CLI (`ddflow config <knob> <value> [--local]`) and MCP (`ddflow_configure`, including the local layer; an agent changing it over MCP is reported to the operator). Per D-review-budget (3). Run the named reviewer gates in parallel over the same diff (chunking computed once; each gate keeps its own prompt, recording, family-independence rules and triage); the output is grouped per gate; one gate failing to run (unavailable) does not hide the other; each counts one round against its own budget. Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Don't poll a roborev job beyond about 10 minutes before recording it partial.' (and: 'by default for all ddflow projects too, but make sure user or mcp can configure this behavior'). Measured (research R-task-time, slow2): roborev run median 3.4 min, p90 9.5, max 17; an agent gave up a job at 25 min (B-prompt-autocapture gate.partial) and polling/waiting time is a large part of the ~250 min/day attributed to the standards gate. The agent-facing driver text (implement-phase.md, per-agent deltas, templates/prompts) says: enqueue without --wait, check at most ~10 minutes, then record partial. Never records `passed` for an unfinished job (rule: a tool that could not finish is not a pass). The behaviour is a SHIPPED DEFAULT for every project (config dataclass default, not a value in this repository's config.toml) and is changeable at every layer: shared .ddflow/config.toml, machine-local .ddflow/local/config.toml (`ddflow config --local`), env override, CLI (`ddflow config <knob> <value> [--local]`) and MCP (`ddflow_configure`, including the local layer; an agent changing it over MCP is reported to the operator). The tools/list byte budget must stay green. README and config --explain document default and how to change it (D-readme-current). Acceptance (failing-first): a fake roborev job that never finishes yields a partial gate at the limit (use a tiny roborev_poll_s in the test), job id recorded; finishing later upgrades it on verify; 0 = unlimited; knob settable via config --local and ddflow_configure; driver docs updated; README updated.

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Do show who is locking a file, but also put a limit on the lock in terms of time so if the lock lasts too long we allow someone else to edit the file and then correct the issues at merge, and in case there are merge issues the unit tests shall be run to verify the merging correction didn't create own bugs and recessions. All of this behavior should be configurable, including timeout, unlocking, via config, cli or mcp.' Chosen over the two options in the earlier analysis (visibility OR early release): BOTH. (1) Visibility: who holds which file, since when, who waits (B-lease-hold-visibility). (2) A time limit on a hold: [lease].hold_max_s (default 3600; 0 = never, the old behaviour). After that age a lease on CONTENDED globs (someone waits or claims) becomes BREAKABLE: another agent's claim of an overlapping item is allowed, recorded as a lease.overlap (holder, claimant, files, age) and shown in both agents' briefs; the original holder is never evicted or deleted, it keeps its worktree and branch. (3) Reconciliation at merge: the first branch to merge wins the file; the second merges main in; if that merge conflicts, or both touched the same file, ddflow records merge.reconciled with the files, REFUSES to complete until the full unit suite (and the slow scenarios when their path is touched) has run on the reconciled tree and passed, and the gate evidence names the reconciled files and the suite run. Reconciliation can never be skipped silently (--force --reason is the recorded exception). (4) All configurable: [lease].hold_max_s, [lease].break_on_timeout (default true), [lease].hold_warn_s, [lease].reconcile_tests (default full; full|affected|off); CLI `ddflow config lease.hold_max_s N [--local]`, `ddflow lease break <item> --reason` / `ddflow lease keep <item> --for N` (operator can unlock early or extend), MCP ddflow_configure for the knobs and the break/keep actions (agents may extend only their own hold; breaking another's is operator or timeout only). Defaults are the shipped defaults for every project. Risks accepted and mitigations: two branches edit one file -> textual conflicts are caught by git, semantic conflicts by the mandatory post-reconcile suite; never evict a live holder; a break is a visible event, never silent.
data.title: Hot-file locks are visible and time-limited: after hold_max_s a contended lease is breakable, conflicts are reconciled at merge and the full suite must pass on the reconciled tree; all configurable

[upgrade].backup = local | snapshot | none (shipped default local): local copies the files an upgrade is about to change into .ddflow/backups/<timestamp>-<from>-to-<to>/ (git-ignored, not shared across machines, pruned by [upgrade].backup_keep); snapshot makes a git commit (or tag) of the affected files before applying (shared, durable, undone with git revert; refused with a clear message if the tree is dirty or there is no git); also selectable per run with ddflow upgrade --apply --snapshot. The README explains both options, the default, what each costs and how to restore (ddflow upgrade --restore <backup>). Configurable via config, CLI and MCP. data.title: Upgrade backups are local by default (.ddflow/backups, git-ignored); a git-tracked snapshot is an option; both explained in the README

data.body:
--apply <category,...>|all. Before ANY write: snapshot every file it will touch to .ddflow/backups/<ts>-<from>-to-<to>/ (local, git-ignored) and print the git diff command; driver docs and rules blocks get a version+body-sha256 header (like export docs) so hand edits are detected and the file is moved aside (.local-edits) or refused, never silently overwritten (also fix adopt --refresh-docs to use it). Dangling git-hook binary is repaired by hooks install. Idempotent: second apply is a no-op. Appends upgrade.applied (from, to, categories, backup) so replay explains it. Config-default changes are never auto-applied: they are listed with 'pin old behaviour: ddflow config --set X old' and recorded when the operator acknowledges.
Failing-first: local edit in driver doc survives to .local-edits and is reported; apply twice = identical tree; kill mid-apply leaves backup and a re-runnable plan; replay shows the upgrade event.

OPERATOR DECISION D-upgrade-backups (2026-10-03): backups are LOCAL by default ([upgrade].backup = local|snapshot|none, default local, .ddflow/backups git-ignored, [upgrade].backup_keep); a git-tracked snapshot is the opt-in (--snapshot or [upgrade].backup = snapshot; refused clearly on a dirty tree or without git); `ddflow upgrade --restore <backup>`; configurable via config, CLI and MCP. README MUST explain both options, the default, what each costs and how to restore (acceptance: a test asserts the README section exists and names both).
